notes: Upgraded server.py from a single-threaded http.server.HTTPServer to ThreadingHTTPServer. Previously, any slow operation (a harvest, an external enrichment fetch, a large deliverable render) blocked every other client -- including simple polling requests like /api/sync-status -- until it finished, sometimes causing outright connection failures. Request handlers were already safe for this: each opens and closes its own short-lived SQLite connection per call rather than sharing one across requests, and the few pieces of shared mutable state (the sync-in-progress flag, the enrichment scheduler's running flags) were already guarded with threading.Lock -- so this was a safe drop-in swap, not a rewrite. Verified live: 5 concurrent requests fired during an active harvest all completed successfully instead of hanging or erroring.
